# 1 Samuel Chapter 23 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 163-164 | **Source Images:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1SA_023_page_001.jpg, 1SA_023_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And they told David, saying, "Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are plundering the threshing floors."

**2** And David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I go and strike these Philistines?" And the LORD said to David, "Go and strike the Philistines and save Keilah."

**3** And David's men said to him, "Behold, we are afraid here in Judah. How much more then if we go to Keilah against the battle lines of the Philistines?"

**4** And David inquired of the LORD once more. And the LORD answered him and said, "Arise, go down to Keilah, for I am giving the Philistines into your hand."

**5** And David and his men went to Keilah and fought against the Philistines. And he drove off their livestock and struck them with a great blow. And David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

**6** And it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, that the ephod came down in his hand.

**7** And it was told to Saul that David had come to Keilah. And Saul said, "God has delivered him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town with gates and bars."

**8** And Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.

**9** And David knew that Saul was devising evil against him. And he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod here."

**10** And David said, "O LORD, God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah, to destroy the city on my account.

**11** Will the lords of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? O LORD, God of Israel, please tell your servant." And the LORD said, "He will come down."

**12** And David said, "Will the lords of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?" And the LORD said, "They will surrender you."

**13** And David and his men arose — about six hundred men — and they went out from Keilah and wandered wherever they could go. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, and he ceased going out.

**14** And David dwelt in the wilderness, in the strongholds, and he dwelt in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God did not give him into his hand.

**15** And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his soul. And David was in the wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.

**16** And Jonathan the son of Saul arose and went to David at Horesh, and he strengthened his hand in God.

**17** And he said to him, "Do not be afraid, for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you. And you shall reign over Israel, and I shall be second to you. And even Saul my father knows this."

**18** And the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.

**19** And the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, which is south of Jeshimon?

**20** Now then, O king, come down according to all the desire of your soul to come down, and it shall be our part to surrender him into the hand of the king."

**21** And Saul said, "Blessed are you by the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.

**22** Go now, make yet more sure. Know and see his place where his foot is — who has seen him there — for it has been told me that he is very cunning.

**23** See and learn of all the hiding places where he hides himself, and return to me with certain knowledge. Then I will go with you. And it shall be, if he is in the land, that I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah."

**24** And they arose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of Jeshimon.

**25** And Saul and his men went to seek him. And they told David, and he went down to the rock and dwelt in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.

**26** And Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain. And David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were encircling David and his men to capture them.

**27** And a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid upon the land."

**28** So Saul turned back from pursuing David and went to meet the Philistines. Therefore they called that place the Rock of Division.

**29** And David went up from there and dwelt in the strongholds of En-gedi.

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes

Chapter 23 is structured by David's repeated consultations of the LORD through the ephod (vv. 2, 4, 9-12), contrasted with Saul's misreading of providence (v. 7). The binary oracle format — yes/no questions answered by the LORD — reflects the Urim and Thummim consultation technique.

In verse 6, the note that the ephod "came down in his hand" (יָרַד אֵפוֹד בְּיָדוֹ) is syntactically ambiguous; this translation takes it as a circumstantial clause explaining that Abiathar brought the ephod with him when he fled.

Verse 16 contains the theologically significant phrase וַיְחַזֵּק אֶת־יָדוֹ בֵּאלֹהִים (vaychazzeq et-yado be'lohim), "he strengthened his hand in God" — Jonathan's final meeting with David, a scene of remarkable self-abnegation (v. 17). The term נַפְשְׁךָ (nafshekha) in verse 20 is rendered "your soul" per convention.

The סֶלַע הַמַּחְלְקוֹת (sela' hammahlequot, "Rock of Division") in verse 28 commemorates the dramatic near-capture: the name derives from חלק ("to divide/separate"), marking the providential moment when Saul was diverted by the Philistine raid.

— LOGOS (Λόγος), translated from the Leningrad Codex (B19A)
